open_points.subject: FlowActivation creation for a proven read-only flow (K-08, primary actions, M18)
open_points.text: K-08: "A read-only flow is activated by the kernel once proven"; primary action: "activate a flow | agent or owner asks; the kernel activates a proven read-only version at once"; M18 source: "The kernel, after proof and, for effectful versions, the owner."
open_points.question: When exactly is a FlowActivation record created for a proven read-only flow: automatically at successful proof, only when the activate action is called, or both?
options: Create FlowActivation automatically as part of compose-and-prove when proof is proven and highest_effect_class is read.
Create FlowActivation only through the activate action; for read-only requests the kernel is the recorded activator.
Auto-create on proof, and later activate calls just return the existing active version without creating a new activation.
open_points.default_guess: Create FlowActivation automatically immediately after successful proof for read-only versions.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile byte access action (M22)
open_points.text: M22: "Read by ... the owner's inspection read of its bytes (A10 rule 2; the State 5 operation `read_spooled_file`)"; State 0 primary actions list has no action that explicitly reads spooled file bytes.
open_points.question: What State-1 product action reads SpooledFile bytes, and who is allowed to invoke it?
options: Define an owner-only action to read spooled file bytes (separate from trace reading).
Treat byte access as part of existing inspect/read-trace actions.
No direct byte-read action; bytes are only used internally for execution and capture.
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate owner-only byte-read action for spooled files.

open_points.subject: Approval mismatch handling when a standing grant exists (owner decision 18 vs M24 lifecycle)
open_points.text: Owner decision 18: "Any difference at send ... asks again." M24 lifecycle: "An approved, unused approval whose `request_digest` no longer matches ... is simply no authority for that send; the kernel then sends under an active grant when one applies, otherwise requests a new approval."
open_points.question: If the request changed and a previous approval no longer matches, but a standing grant is active for that node/version, must the kernel ask again or may it send under the grant?
options: May send under the active standing grant without a new per-run approval.
Must always request a fresh owner approval when request_digest differs, even if a standing grant exists.
Treat request mismatch as invalidating standing grant authority for that send and require approval.
open_points.default_guess: May send under the active standing grant; otherwise request a new approval.
